userImpact: Users must manually pan/drag from the city center to their exact location with no 'use my location' and no address search, which is slow and error-prone; and because the pin is not validated, an address can be saved with the default coordinate that has nothing to do with the typed address — so a phone-coordinated delivery may target the wrong point.
recommendation: Add a geolocation ('موقعیت فعلی من') button and an address/geocode search; ideally reverse-geocode the pin into the text field (and vice-versa). At minimum require the pin to be moved from the default before saving.

title: Stop the fixed submit CTA from occluding form fields and the keyboard
evidence: Every form pins its submit as position:fixed;bottom:80px (refill L463, used L518, checkout L592) above the fixed bottom nav. The ground-truth capture reports the refill CTA overlapping/covering the contact-phone field. Refill reserves 170px bottom padding (L389) vs a CTA topping out ~130px, so raw padding does not explain it — the trigger is the short/no-scroll configuration and the mobile keyboard.
userImpact: On the refill form a field ends up hidden behind the floating CTA, so the user cannot see what they are typing; when the on-screen keyboard opens, a position:fixed CTA can also float over the focused input, compounding the problem across all form screens.
recommendation: Prefer an inline CTA at the end of the scroll (or a sticky footer that participates in layout) rather than position:fixed; if kept fixed, guarantee scroll space ≥ CTA height + nav height + safe-area and handle the keyboard (hide/reposition the CTA on focus).

title: Adopt a shared form UX standard (FormField + submit contract)
evidence: Each form re-implements label divs, error divs, and ad-hoc submit handlers with no common structure; there is no <form> element anywhere, OTP has no auto-submit at 6 digits (verifyOtp L216 requires a manual tap even though onOtp truncates to 6), and single-field steps cannot be submitted with the keyboard Go/Enter key.
userImpact: Inconsistency compounds every issue above (validation timing, required markers, a11y, error focus differ per screen) and makes fixes N-times the work; users also lose small efficiencies like auto-submitting a 6-digit OTP or pressing Go to send.
recommendation: Build one FormField (label+for, required marker, inline validate-on-blur with live-clear, aria-describedby error with role=alert, valid state) and one submit contract (disabled/pending, focus-first-error, draft retention). Wrap steps in <form onsubmit> for Enter/Go, and auto-submit OTP when 6 digits are entered.

title: Persian search matching is brittle: no ZWNJ, space, or digit normalization
evidence: script_2.js L330-332 — query filter only does s.q.replace(/ي/g,'ی').replace(/ك/g,'ک') then a raw .includes() over title+desc+gas. Product content uses ZWNJ/نیم‌فاصله ('اکسیژن‌ساز', 'یک‌بارمصرف', 'پلمب‌شده') and Persian digits ('۴۰ لیتری').
userImpact: A Persian user searching 'اکسیژن ساز' (normal space) gets zero results because the product is stored as 'اکسیژن‌ساز' (ZWNJ); '40' fails to match '۴۰'; a device with an Arabic keyboard's alef-variants also misses. Users conclude the shop doesn't stock the item and abandon. This is the single highest-impact i18n defect — search silently fails for the most natural Persian queries.
recommendation: Add a shared normalize() applied symmetrically to BOTH the query and the searchable text: fold ي→ی, ك→ک, ه/ة, collapse ZWNJ(U+200C) and all space variants to a single space (or strip them for matching), and run deFa() so Persian and ASCII digits are unified before includes(). Consider matching per-token instead of a single substring.

title: Emergency hotline number is the same as the logged-in user's own phone
evidence: markup_only.html L383 shows the services '24/7 emergency order' card phone as 0912 845 7455; script_2.js L72 auto-login seeds the user with phone: '0912 845 7455' — byte-identical. That same number is echoed back in the profile header (userPhone, markup L650).
userImpact: The app boots logged-in with this seeded profile, so a user reads the shop's 'سفارش فوری کپسول اکسیژن — شبانه‌روزی' hotline and sees literally their own number, which also appears in their profile. It reads as a copy/paste placeholder and directly undermines the emergency-availability trust message on a medical-oxygen product — the one place credibility matters most.
recommendation: Use a distinct, real business hotline constant for the services card (and ideally a tel: link so it dials). Never reuse the demo user's seeded phone as store content; source both from separate config.

title: Leftover prototype and English-leak copy is shipped in the Persian UI
evidence: markup_only.html L343 'کد نمونه برای این پیش‌نمایش: 123456'; L179 mono label 'product photo · تصویر محصول' on the detail hero; L401/L484 'IMG' tiles; L681 footer 'نسخه پیش‌نمایش PWA'; script_2.js L486-487 toasts 'افزودن آدرس با MapPicker در نمونه بعدی' / 'انتخاب پین روی نقشه (Neshan) در نمونه بعدی'.
userImpact: End users see the hardcoded OTP, English placeholder strings ('product photo', 'IMG'), 'preview/PWA' scaffolding, and 'in the next sample' TODO toasts. In a Persian medical-commerce context this scaffolding reads as unfinished/untrustworthy and mixes English into an otherwise all-Persian RTL surface.
recommendation: Gate demo strings (OTP hint, 'نمونه بعدی' toasts, preview footer) behind a build/prototype flag; replace 'product photo'/'IMG' with real imagery or a localized alt caption; remove or Persian-localize 'PWA'. Do a copy pass to strip all dev-facing text before production.

title: Grand-total label differs between cart and checkout; shipping row labels a method as a cost
evidence: Cart summary: 'مبلغ قابل پرداخت' (markup L298) and 'هزینه ارسال' whose value is 'هماهنگی تلفنی' (L296). Checkout summary: the same grand total is named 'مبلغ نهایی' (L589) and adds an 'اقلام سفارش' row (L583) the cart lacks.
userImpact: Across two adjacent money screens the payable total is named two different things (مبلغ قابل پرداخت vs مبلغ نهایی), which erodes confidence at the most trust-sensitive step. 'هزینه ارسال' literally means shipping COST but shows a method ('هماهنگی تلفنی'), a label/value mismatch that can read as a hidden/unknown charge.
recommendation: Standardize one term for the payable amount app-wide (e.g. 'مبلغ قابل پرداخت'). Relabel the shipping line to 'نحوه ارسال' (method) or 'هزینه ارسال: هنگام تحویل' so the value matches the label. Mirror the same summary rows on both cart and checkout.

title: Page-title typeface is inconsistent across screens (Baloo h1 vs Vazirmatn div)
evidence: Top-tab screens use real headings → Baloo: products h1 L112, cart h1 L253, services h1 L359, profile h1 L621, detail title h1 L187. Back-chevron sub-pages render the title as a plain div → Vazirmatn: refill L394, usedSale L477, checkout L551, orders L691, requests L723, addresses L755, wishlist L807, auth L321 (all `<div style="font-weight:900;font-size:17px">`). CSS applies Baloo only to h1,h2.
userImpact: The same visual role (screen title) switches font family and apparent weight depending on which route you're on, so the header looks different as the user navigates — an inconsistent, less-polished brand feel that's especially visible in Persian where Baloo and Vazirmatn letterforms differ markedly.
recommendation: Pick one title treatment. Either promote sub-page titles to h1/h2 (Baloo) or, given the Baloo weight problem below, standardize all titles on Vazirmatn with a defined weight/size token. Don't mix per route.

title: Baloo Bhaijaan 2 has no usable weight axis — heading weight hierarchy collapses
evidence: style_1.css declares 16 @font-face but resolves to only 4 unique woff2 URLs (grep-confirmed: each of c4acad6a…, 9e5423b7…, 4de9721d…, 39312691… reused 4×), one per subset shared across weights 500/600/700/800. CSS maps only h1,h2 to Baloo; markup sets font-weight:900 on hero h1 (L60) and 800 on section h2 (L84) — 900 isn't even declared for Baloo.
userImpact: Every Baloo heading renders at one physical weight regardless of the 500–900 values in the markup, so intended emphasis (hero title vs section header) is flat. Worse, adjacent prices set to font-weight:900 render in Vazirmatn's real 900, so a Baloo 'heading' can look LIGHTER than the numbers beside it — an inverted hierarchy.
recommendation: Ship a real Baloo variable font or the distinct static weights, or drop Baloo for headings and use Vazirmatn (which has 9 genuine weights) with an explicit type scale. Remove reliance on font-weight:900 for Baloo since it's undeclared.

title: Negative letter-spacing and inconsistent line-heights degrade Persian heading typography
evidence: style_3.css h1,h2 rule: letter-spacing:-.4px; line-height:1.28. Inline overrides fight it: hero h1 line-height:1.5 (markup L60), detail h1 line-height:1.6 (L187), body container line-height:1.7 (L31).
userImpact: Negative tracking on a cursive, connected script like Persian works against the font's built-in joining/kerning and can crowd or clip glyphs and diacritics; the tight 1.28 line-height risks clipping ascenders/hamza. Three different heading line-heights make vertical rhythm inconsistent between screens.
recommendation: Remove letter-spacing for Arabic-script text (scope any tracking to Latin-only via :lang or a utility class), and standardize a single heading line-height (~1.4–1.5) rather than per-instance inline overrides.

title: Medical/regulatory trust copy is absent for a medical-oxygen storefront
evidence: Products are 'اکسیژن طبی' (medical oxygen) and pressure cylinders (script_2.js L31-54). Descriptions carry some trust signals ('تست هیدرواستاتیک معتبر', 'پر و پلمب', 'گارانتی') but there is no licensing/authorization (مجوز), prescription/eligibility note, safety-handling guidance, returns/refund policy, or purity-certificate wording anywhere; footer is only 'امداد اکسیژن تهران · نسخه پیش‌نمایش PWA' (L681).
userImpact: For a regulated medical gas, buyers (and often regulators) expect authorization, safe-handling, and prescription/eligibility statements. Their absence lowers perceived legitimacy and may create compliance exposure for real deployment.
recommendation: Add a trust layer: license/authorization line and logo, a short safety-handling note on cylinder detail pages, prescription/eligibility disclaimer for اکسیژن طبی, and a returns/warranty policy link. Localize all of it in the established formal register.

title: User-entered and long Persian strings can overflow chips, rows, and the tab bar
evidence: Address title input has no maxlength (markup L886) yet the address-card title row (L764-772) lays out title + 'پیش‌فرض' badge + 3-dot menu with a flex:1 spacer and no min-width:0/ellipsis on the title span. Status pills like 'در انتظار بررسی' (requestsList, L737) and bottom-nav labels 'محصولات'/'پروفایل' at font-size:10px in repeat(5,1fr) (L921) have no white-space:nowrap/overflow handling.
userImpact: A long address title pushes the default badge and options menu off-screen or wraps awkwardly; the 'در انتظار بررسی' pill can wrap inside its rounded shape; nav labels can wrap/clip on sub-360px devices — all more likely in Persian where words don't break mid-token.
recommendation: Cap adTitle length and add min-width:0 + overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap to title spans; give status pills white-space:nowrap; allow nav labels to shrink or ellipsize. Test with the longest real labels.

title: Inconsistent terminology and loanwords for staff and repeated concepts
evidence: Staff referred to four ways: 'کارشناسان' (script_2.js L193 inquire toast), 'همکاران ما' (success note L611), 'اپراتور' and 'تکنسین' (formSuccess refill note L601). Refill delivery heading 'نوع درخواست ارسال' (markup L421) is awkward vs the cleaner 'زمان و روش ارسال' used at checkout (L570). Wishlist empty-state says 'آیکن قلب' (L812), an English loanword.
userImpact: Mixing کارشناس/همکار/اپراتور/تکنسین (and Persian vs transliterated loanwords) for the same people, plus varied labels for the same concept, weakens a consistent, trustworthy brand voice — noticeable to native readers.
recommendation: Define a short microcopy glossary (one term for staff, one for delivery method, prefer Persian over اپراتور/تکنسین/آیکن) and apply it across toasts, success notes, and form headings.

title: Discount amount is formatted as a positive number with a trailing minus in RTL
evidence: discLabel = fmt(t.disc) is a positive Persian-digit number (script_2.js L525); templates render '{{ discLabel }}− تومان' (markup L294 cart, L586 checkout), placing the U+2212 minus after the digits and before تومان.
userImpact: The sign sits ambiguously relative to the number in an RTL run ('۵۰۰٬۰۰۰− تومان'), which is non-standard and can read as either negative or a stray dash — sloppy for a money value.
recommendation: Format the discount as a genuine negative via Intl.NumberFormat with signDisplay (or prepend the minus: '−۵۰۰٬۰۰۰ تومان') and wrap the numeric run in <bdi> so the sign stays attached correctly in RTL.

title: Latin runs interpolated into Persian microcopy lack bidi isolation
evidence: authErr string embeds an ASCII phone example inside Persian: 'شماره موبایل معتبر ایران وارد کنید (مثلاً 09123456789)' (script_2.js L211), rendered in a plain error div (markup L331) with no dir/<bdi>. The discount placeholder 'کد تخفیف (مثلاً EMDAD10)' (L285) similarly mixes a Latin token into an RTL field with no isolation.
userImpact: Neutral characters (parentheses, the discount minus) around embedded Latin/numeric runs are direction-ambiguous in RTL and can render on the unexpected side across engines, giving inconsistent, non-localized number/punctuation formatting in the very messages meant to guide the user.
recommendation: Best practice: wrap embedded Latin/number runs in <bdi> (or bracket with U+2066…U+2069 isolates), or use Persian example digits, so formatting is deterministic regardless of engine. Apply the same treatment wherever codes/phones sit inside Persian sentences.

title: Form placeholders and error hints use inconsistent digit systems and helpfulness
evidence: Phone placeholders are ASCII '0912 345 6789' (markup L330/L453/L504) while the price placeholder is Persian 'مثلاً ۲٬۵۰۰٬۰۰۰' (L498). The auth phone error gives a format example (script_2.js L211) but the refill/used phone errors are bare 'شماره موبایل معتبر وارد کنید' (L259/L270); the submit-fail toast 'لطفاً موارد مشخص‌شده را تکمیل کنید' (L261/L275) names neither the field nor a count.
userImpact: Mixed numerals across placeholders on the same form look unpolished, and the generic submit toast forces users to hunt for the offending field — made worse by the known fixed-CTA overlap that hides the phone field. Inconsistent error helpfulness means some fields explain the fix and others don't.
recommendation: Pick one placeholder digit convention (Persian digits are fine even for dir=ltr phone fields since deFa already normalizes input), add the same format hint to every phone error, and make the toast specific (e.g. '۲ مورد نیاز به اصلاح دارد') and scroll to the first error.

title: Fix the fixed-CTA overlapping the contact-phone field on the refill form
evidence: Refill route (markup_only.html): scroll area reserves only padding-bottom 170px (L389) while the primary CTA is position:fixed;bottom:80px (L463); the required 'شماره تماس' input sits at L453. Ground-truth driving the live app confirms the floating button covers this field.
userImpact: On the refill service form the floating 'ثبت درخواست شارژ' button hides the required contact-phone field, so the user cannot see what they are typing into it — a direct path to failed/abandoned service requests.
recommendation: Don't rely on a single cause: (a) raise the scroll padding-bottom to clear nav + CTA + env(safe-area-inset-bottom), AND (b) make the CTA sticky within the scroll flow or listen to window.visualViewport resize to hide/relocate the bar so a focused input is never occluded when the on-screen keyboard opens.

title: Offset every fixed CTA and the toast by the safe-area inset
evidence: Six fixed action bars are hardcoded at bottom:80px (markup L235, L242, L306, L463, L518, L592) and the toast at bottom:88px (L906), but only the bottom nav adds env(safe-area-inset-bottom) (L912). Sheets also bottom-pad a flat 24px with no inset.
userImpact: On notched / home-indicator phones the nav grows taller than the fixed 80px offset, so the primary CTAs and the toast collide with or tuck behind the nav (or sit under the home indicator), making the main action awkward to tap on exactly the devices the PWA targets.
recommendation: Offset each fixed CTA/toast with calc(80px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) (or drive it from a measured nav-height CSS var), and add padding-bottom:env(safe-area-inset-bottom) inside the bottom sheets.

title: Complete the bottom-sheet interaction: swipe-to-dismiss, max-height scroll, safe-area
evidence: Filter sheet (markup L840-861) and address sheet (L864-903) render a 40x4 grabber pill (L844/L868) that implies drag, but dismissal is only scrim-tap (L841/L865) or a button — no touch/pointer drag handler exists (grep: none). Neither sheet sets a max-height or internal scroll; the address-FORM sheet stacks a 190px map (L893) + two inputs + the Save button (L899) with only 24px bottom padding.
userImpact: The grabber is a false affordance — users swipe down to close and nothing happens. Worse, with no max-height/scroll, when the keyboard opens (or on a short viewport) the tall address-form sheet overflows and the 'ذخیره آدرس' Save button is pushed off-screen and unreachable, blocking address creation entirely.
recommendation: Wire the grabber to a swipe/drag-down-to-dismiss gesture, cap the sheet at max-height:85dvh with overflow:auto on the body, pin the Save button in a sticky sheet footer, and add safe-area bottom padding.

title: Remove or make real the fake product carousel (dots imply swipe that does nothing)
evidence: Detail route (markup L178-185): a 220px crosshatch placeholder box plus three indicator dots — the first hardcoded active (background:var(--p)), two inactive — bound to no state, with no swipe handler and no image array. Ground-truth confirms there are no real images and no swipe.
userImpact: The three dots signal a swipeable photo gallery, so users swipe the image and tap the dots expecting more views and get zero response — a broken affordance that also undermines trust for higher-consideration medical/industrial purchases.
recommendation: Until real photos exist, drop the dot indicator so nothing implies a gallery. When images ship, build a swipeable track with state-bound, tappable dots (active index in state) and lazy-loaded images.

title: Enlarge sub-44px tap targets and add touch-action:manipulation to steppers/buttons
evidence: Cart qty steppers are 28x28 with a 4px gap inside a 3px-pad pill (markup L273-276); detail steppers 32x32 (L196-198); cart remove 32x32 (L278); the photo-tile remove ✕ is 22x22 offset -6px so it hangs partly off the tile (L402/L485); the address kebab is 32x32 (L770). No touch-action:manipulation is set anywhere (grep).
userImpact: All sit below the ~44px comfortable thumb target; the tightly-spaced +/− invite mis-taps (decrementing/removing the wrong way), and the tiny off-edge ✕ is easy to miss. Rapid +/− tapping can also fire the browser's double-tap-to-zoom, jerking the view.
recommendation: Raise interactive targets to >=44px (or add transparent hit-padding), widen the +/− spacing, move the tile ✕ fully onto the tile, and add touch-action:manipulation to steppers and small buttons to suppress double-tap zoom.

title: Add an in-flight/disabled guard on submit CTAs to prevent latent double-submit
evidence: placeOrder (script_2.js L308 / CTA markup L594), submitRefill (L253 / L465), submitUsed (L265 / L520) and sendOtp/verifyOtp (markup L332/L344) never set a disabled/in-flight flag; today only the synchronous route swap unmounts the button before a second tap can land.
userImpact: The prototype only masks duplicates because submission is instantaneous. The moment these become real async network calls, a double-tap or a slow response will place duplicate orders, duplicate service requests, and duplicate OTP sends.
recommendation: Introduce an isSubmitting flag: on tap, disable the CTA (its glow already drops via the existing [disabled] rule), show a spinner, ignore re-entrant calls, and re-enable on success/error.

title: Raise input font-size to >=16px and add tel autofill + OTP auto-submit
evidence: Inputs are under 16px throughout — products search 13px (markup L116), discount 13px (L285), auth phone 15px (L330), refill phone 14px (L453), checkout phone 14px (L568), used phone 14px (L504), plus 13px textareas. No input has an explicit type (grep) — phone fields rely on inputmode='numeric' only, with no autocomplete='tel'. The OTP field has autocomplete='one-time-code' but only submits on the button tap (verifyOtp, L344), not on completion.
userImpact: iOS Safari auto-zooms whenever you focus an input under 16px, jerking the whole layout and reflowing the fixed bars on every field focus. Phone fields miss type='tel'/autocomplete='tel' autofill, and users must manually reach for 'تأیید' after typing the 6th OTP digit.
recommendation: Set all inputs/textareas to font-size >=16px; give phone fields type='tel' + autocomplete='tel'; auto-submit the OTP once six digits are entered.

title: Support native back: History API, edge-swipe, and a thumb-reachable back control
evidence: Every sub-page's only back affordance is a 40x40 chevron pinned to the top-start corner (e.g. detail L170, checkout L548, refill L391, orders L688). There is no history/popstate/pushState and no edge-swipe handler (grep); a route change is just window.scrollTo(0,0) (script_2.js L78).
userImpact: On a large phone the top-corner back button is the hardest one-handed reach, and because routing never touches browser history, an OS/browser back gesture exits the app instead of going back a screen. Users must stretch to the top corner on every single sub-screen.
recommendation: Drive routes through the History API (pushState + popstate) so the native back gesture and hardware Back navigate within the app, add an edge-swipe-back gesture, and/or mirror a back control into the thumb zone.

title: Restore list scroll position when returning from a detail page
evidence: componentDidUpdate unconditionally resets scroll to top on any route change (script_2.js L76-78); there is no per-route scroll memory.
userImpact: Scrolling deep into the products or orders list, opening an item, then tapping back dumps the user at the very top of the list every time — a classic mobile annoyance that makes browsing a long catalog tedious and disorienting.
recommendation: Remember the scroll offset per route (at minimum for list->detail->back) and restore it on return; only scroll-to-top when navigating forward to a genuinely new page.

title: Treat the animated aurora + per-card backdrop-blur as a scroll/typing perf risk
evidence: Aurora blobs are position:fixed with will-change:transform animating infinitely (style_3.css L42-44); every --sur/--sur2 surface gets backdrop-filter:blur(16-18px) saturate(1.3) (L46-48); and the single monolithic Component re-renders and re-runs manageMaps() DOM work on every keystroke/state bump (script_2.js L76-80). No jank was measured — this is a mechanism-based risk.
userImpact: On low/mid-range Android, scrolling long lists of frosted cards over the continuously-moving blurred background, and typing (each keystroke re-renders everything and re-runs map management), risks dropped frames and input lag.
recommendation: Limit simultaneously-blurred surfaces (use a solid --sur fill on list cards), pause/park the aurora during active scroll, debounce the search filter, and gate manageMaps() so it only runs on map-bearing routes and on actual coordinate changes.

title: Set overscroll-behavior so an accidental pull-to-refresh can't wipe in-memory state
evidence: No overscroll-behavior or touch-action is set anywhere (grep); the scroll root is the document body (wrapper min-height:100dvh, markup L31); and all state is purely in-memory with no persistence (reload loses cart, auth, and orders).
userImpact: An accidental over-scroll past the top can trigger the browser/PWA pull-to-refresh, reloading the app and silently wiping the cart, login session, and order history in the middle of a checkout or service-request flow.
recommendation: Add overscroll-behavior-y:contain to the scroll root (disabling pull-to-refresh), and persist cart/auth to storage so a reload is never destructive.

title: Give card/row taps a pressed state and add haptic confirmation on key actions
evidence: The large tappables are plain <div onclick> — product cards (markup L89, L132), delivery-method options (L424), sort rows (L849), address-pick rows (L873) — so the global button:active{transform:translateY(1px)} (style_3.css L53) never applies to them, and there is no navigator.vibrate anywhere (grep).
userImpact: Tapping a product card or option row produces no pressed-state and no tactile feedback, so during the instant-but-unanimated route swap the tap feels dead and users re-tap. Confirmations like add-to-cart, order-placed, and validation errors are also silent.
recommendation: Use real <button>s (or add :active/:focus-visible pressed styling + role='button' + tabindex) for card/row taps, set a branded -webkit-tap-highlight-color, and fire a short navigator.vibrate() on add-to-cart, successful submit, and validation errors.

title: Scroll to and focus the first invalid field on failed form submit
evidence: submitRefill/submitUsed set per-field errors but surface only a generic toast 'لطفاً موارد مشخص‌شده را تکمیل کنید' (script_2.js L261/L275); the submit CTA is bottom-fixed while the first required field (e.g. the photo uploader at the top of refill, markup L397) is far off-screen on these long forms.
userImpact: After tapping the bottom-pinned submit, the user gets a vague toast but the actual invalid field is scrolled out of view with no indication where it is, leaving them hunting for what to fix.
recommendation: On validation failure, scroll and focus the first errored field into view and have the toast name that first issue; validate on blur so errors surface before the user reaches the bottom.

title: Make destructive removes reversible with an Undo action instead of silent auto-toasts
evidence: Cart item removal deletes immediately (script_2.js L392) as does address deletion (deleteAddr L280); toasts are pointer-events:none, auto-dismiss after 2.4s, and carry no action button (markup L906-908, script L160).
userImpact: Combined with the small remove/✕ targets, one accidental tap permanently drops a cart line or a saved address with no recovery — especially costly for an address, which required placing a map pin to create.
recommendation: Make destructive actions reversible: show an actionable snackbar with a 'بازگردانی' (Undo) button and a short grace delay before the delete commits.
